Al 2010 reported lead at 55 µg/kg (mean ± 31 SD) in kidney beans, as sold from Legume, Riyadh city markets, May 2009.<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> authors 2017 reported cadmium at 70 µg/kg (mean ± 60 SD) and total arsenic at 60 µg/kg (mean ± 30 SD) in kidney beans, as sold from open markets, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2017-levels-dietary-intake-and-health-risk-of-potentially|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2017-levels-dietary-intake-and-health-risk-of-potentially">Levels, dietary intake, and health risk of potentially toxic metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2017-levels-dietary-intake-and-health-risk-of-potentially">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the kidney beans came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of kidney beans, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:kidney-beans-6bb3b15e1a01:8dac5ff2bda2"><summary>HMI kidney beans Pb reference · Kidney beans, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:kidney-beans-6bb3b15e1a01:8dac5ff2bda2"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI kidney beans Pb reference · Kidney beans, as sold. Kidney beans, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤2.2</td><td>0.9–22.5 (bounded)</td><td>3.1–40 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤2.2</td><td>0.9–40 (bounded)</td><td>3.1–40 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>10 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>10</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for kidney beans, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for kidney beans, as sold on this basis in the completed kidney beans ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:kidney-beans-6bb3b15e1a01:8dac5ff2bda2</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:kidney-beans-560bf750d106:3f284122c9aa"><summary>HMI kidney beans Pb reference · Kidney beans, as sold, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:kidney-beans-560bf750d106:3f284122c9aa"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI kidney beans Pb reference · Kidney beans, as sold, dry weight. The HMI reference for lead in kidney beans, canned pools 4 subgroup units from 2 sampling families, with a median of below 4 µg/kg and a middle half spanning below 4 (lower quartile) and below 4 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Spungen JH, et al. · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Infants&#39; and young children&#39;s dietary exposures to lead and cadmium: FDA total diet study 2018-2020</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For lead in kidney beans, as sold, the reference median was between 0.9 and 22.5 µg/kg, with a middle half from below 2.2 to between 3.1 and 40 µg/kg across 10 units.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For lead in kidney beans, as sold, the reference median was below 5.08 µg/kg, with a middle half from below 5 to between 2.58 and 7.58 µg/kg across 4 units.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, kidney beans, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (0.599 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (3.1 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed kidney beans in the same study and group. Kidney beans, canned (Legume, Riyadh city markets, May 2009) had lead lower at 47 µg/kg, against 55 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (kidney beans, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" </div>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-kidney-beans" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-kidney-beans" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in kidney beans?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in kidney beans?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, kidney beans, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (0.599 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (3.1 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-kidney-beans" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-kidney-beans" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in kidney beans?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in kidney beans?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same kidney beans.<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Kidney beans, canned (Legume, Riyadh city markets, May 2009) had lead lower at 47 µg/kg, against 55 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (kidney beans, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
